tactic.scheme: Per two-sided node P, two safe forward rules: P_of_dual : C.dual.P → C.P (shrinks the term), and P_dual : C.P → C.dual.P with the aesop rule pattern `Causality.dual C`. A pattern rule takes its C from a subterm `C.dual` of the goal or of a hypothesis (Aesop/Index/RulePattern.lean getInGoal; Forward/State/Initial.lean and ApplyGoalDiff.lean scan hyps and target), so it fires only for a C whose time reversal is already in sight. Termination: no rule creates a new `t.dual` subterm (P_dual writes t.dual only for a t.dual present; P_of_dual, the generated rules and the introductions write terms already present), so the subjects of a saturation are the finitely many subterms of goal and hypotheses. The one-sided nodes get only the introductions C.P_future ∧ C.dual.P_future → C.P_twoSided. Pair nodes: the same two rules, pattern on the first causality.
tactic.why_not_plain_mpr: Measured: an unguarded forward `C.IsCausal → C.dual.IsCausal` makes `(h : C.IsCausal) ⊢ C.Tarentin` fail with 'maximum rule application depth (30) was reached' instead of exhaustive search. Aesop's forward deduplication is reducible-rigid defeq (RuleTac/Forward.lean isRedundant, Forward/Match.lean), and Causality.dual is not reducible, so C.dual.dual.P is a new hypothesis.
tactic.alternative_tried: A guard class `TimeSign (C : Causality M) (b : outParam Bool)` with a high-priority instance for C.dual flipping b and a low-priority base instance `TimeSign C false`; the rule `[TimeSign C false] → C.P → C.dual.P`. It works (the outParam makes synthesis keep the first answer, so C.dual never falls back on the base instance) and derives the same closure, but transports every fact of every causal_ladder call: the Test.lean replay went from 4.5 s to 6.3 s. The pattern guard costs nothing when no C.dual is in sight, and needs no class. Not shipped.
tactic.idle_check: trace.aesop.forward on `(h : C.IsCausal) ⊢ C.Tarentin` with Dual imported: isCausal_dual is selected for premise h but never has a complete match (no pattern instance), so nothing is transported.

closure_pairs.shipped_in_DualTest: 425 examples. Hand-written 24 (21 derived, 3 not derived): more than one reversal (C.dual.dual, C.dual.dual.dual), the introductions, causally_open_future ⇏ its past form (one-way membrane), le_nested and curve_nested both ways and LeNested C C' ⇏ LeNested C.dual C', standing-instance rules across reversal (T1: strongly_causal ⇒ is_causal of C.dual; T2+second countable: globally_hyperbolic ∧ tarentin ⇒ time_function of C.dual), the half-lit line's eleven positive dual facts as one conjunction, its ⇏ C.dual.CausallyOpenFuture, a term argument, two negations read backwards. Generated 401: 56 derived cross pairs, 7 conjunctive rules used on C.dual with their two-sided premises on C (e.g. absolutely_minimal(C) ∧ locally_causally_open_future(C.dual) ⇒ causally_open_future(C.dual)), 338 refuted cross pairs (all 275 P(C) ⇏ Q(C.dual), and the 63 P(C.dual) ⇏ Q(C) with a one-sided end). Only refuted pairs are shipped as negatives, so DualTest cannot go stale as the ladder grows; a derived example can, if an emitted edge is withdrawn or gains an `under`. `python3 -I campaign/T-tac-ladder-dual/dual_closure.py shipped X` reproduces DualTest.lean byte for byte (checked).

aesop_could_not: Time reversal is entered only where a C.dual occurs in the goal or a hypothesis (the pattern). A goal about C from hypotheses about C never goes through C.dual. Nothing is lost on the current ladder (no same-side pair needs it), but an edge that is not invariant under time reversal could make such a detour needed.

C.dual.dual is not normalised to C (simp is off, Causality.dual is not reducible). A hypothesis on C.dual.dual is shrunk by the P_of_dual rules; a goal on C.dual.dual is reached by transport (its subterms are pattern instances) or by the builtin assumption, which matches up to default-transparency defeq (C.CausallyOpenFuture ⊢ C.dual.dual.CausallyOpenFuture closes that way, not by a rule).

Depth: every forward step counts towards maxRuleApplicationDepth, 30 by default and not set by the causal_ladder macro. Transport doubles a saturation: from seven facts of C, a conjunction of eleven goals about C.dual closes, one of twelve with a C.dual.dual conjunct stops at the depth (measured). Single goals are unaffected; the witnesses already close conjunctions one conjunct at a time.

A one-sided fact is never transported, by design: C.CausallyOpenFuture does not give C.dual.CausallyOpenFuture (refuted by the one-way membrane and the half-lit line); the past form is reached only through a two-sided node or a conjunctive rule on C.dual.

Precausality-level duals: a hypothesis `C.toPrecausality.dual.AbsolutelyMinimal` is not read by the rules (it is not reducibly `C.dual.toPrecausality`, though equal by rfl, Causality.dual_toPrecausality). It closes the goal C.dual.AbsolutelyMinimal by defeq assumption but does not give C.AbsolutelyMinimal (checked).

Pair nodes: the pattern is on the first causality only, mixed facts such as LeNested C.dual C' have no rule, and le_nested ⇒ curve_nested is still not a rule (sort pair), so the dual of a LeNested does not give a CurveNestedOn.

proposals: Integration (for the master): add Causal.Ladder.Dual and Causal.Ladder.DualTest to Causal.lean. Then either (a) have emit-lean write `import Causal.Ladder.Dual` into Rules.lean, so every causal_ladder user reasons across time reversal (no cycle: Dual does not import Rules; cost on non-dual goals 0.2–0.6 s over Test.lean's 352 examples), or (b) leave it opt-in: modules that need it import Causal.Ladder.Dual. (a) is recommended. Dual must never import a witness module (as HalfLitDual), since the witnesses are its users.

Basic.lean: set maxRuleApplicationDepth in the macro (60, say). Forward steps count towards it, and termination does not rest on it (the pattern invariant bounds the saturation; maxRuleApplications := 200 bounds the work). Also mention Causal.Ladder.Dual in its docstring.

Ladder field and emit-lean: a [[property]] key `dual` naming its time-reversal lemma (`Causal.Causality.dual_isCausal`, an iff C.dual.P ↔ C.P) for two-sided nodes, and for a one-sided node `two_sided = "causally_open"` with the introduction's witness. `check` resolves it and checks the layer; emit-lean emits the two wrappers (an aesop rule must be a declaration, so emit-lean writes `theorem … := (dual_P).1 h` lines or the ladder names wrapper theorems) and generates DualTest from the literal closure (dual_closure.py is a stdlib prototype that imports tools/ladder.py). This would make Rules.lean and Dual.lean one generated file and DualTest a generated test that cannot go stale.

kb_proposals: causal_ladder across time reversal: import Causal.Ladder.Dual; a goal about C.dual is closed from facts about C (two-sided nodes transported both ways; the past forms of the one-sided nodes come from the generated rules on C.dual). Transport fires only where a C.dual occurs in the goal or a hypothesis (aesop rule pattern `Causality.dual C`); one-sided facts are never transported (T-tac-ladder-dual).

A forward rule that grows its term (C.P → C.dual.P) loops in aesop, whose deduplication is reducible-rigid: guard it with a rule pattern on the grown subterm, so it fires only where that subterm already occurs. A guard class with an outParam also works but makes every call pay.
aesop's maxRuleApplicationDepth (30) counts forward steps: a long conjunction closed by one causal_ladder can hit it once time reversal doubles the saturation; close conjuncts one at a time.
